purpose: Step & Flow routing index for Windows Update/install and network/DNS symptoms. Codes route to a diagnostic family; they are not treated as a diagnosis.

codes.meaning: Windows Update files/cache may be damaged

codes.first: Confirm the account has administrator access
then: investigate security software only if evidence points there

codes.first: Restart and run Windows Update troubleshooter

codes.meaning: Invalid parameter; can occur in update/install workflows
codes.first: Check free disk space and run the appropriate troubleshooter
then: update component repair only after basic checks

codes.meaning: Update timed out or was interrupted
Secure connection can fail when date/time/time zone is wrong
codes.first: Check date, time, time zone and time synchronization

codes.meaning: Upgrade failure commonly associated with a driver
then: remove unnecessary external devices if appropriate

symptoms: server DNS address could not be found
internet works by IP but not by name

sequence.action: Determine scope: one site, all sites, one PC, or all devices
Inspect current IP configuration; do not change it yet
Check whether the client has a plausible IP address, gateway and configured DNS servers
Test name resolution with nslookup for a public hostname
If evidence points to stale client DNS cache, clear only the DNS cache
If DHCP configuration is invalid, route to DHCP renewal; do not renew a statically configured business PC blindly
Full network reset/netsh reset remains a late-stage branch, never the first response

codes.novice_message: Windows reports an invalid parameter. First we will check simple causes such as free space and the update state.
First check the computer's date, time and time zone. Incorrect time can prevent a secure Windows connection.
This family often points to a driver problem during an upgrade. We will identify the device/driver before changing anything.

router_rules.action: normalize uppercase and exact-match known code; if unknown, route by surrounding words before web/evidence lookup

safety_notes: Do not disable firewall/antivirus as a routine first step.
Do not delete SoftwareDistribution contents before simpler checks/troubleshooter and user confirmation.
Do not replace DNS servers just because a website fails once.
Do not run winsock/TCP-IP reset as the first network action.
For business/domain/static-IP devices, avoid DHCP/network changes without understanding configuration.
